owasp.name: Agent Goal Hijack
owasp.summary: Adversarial inputs manipulate the agent's objectives, causing it to pursue unintended goals.

owasp.name: Tool Misuse & Exploitation
owasp.summary: The agent stays within its privileges but drives legitimate tools in unsafe, unintended ways.

owasp.name: Identity & Privilege Abuse
owasp.summary: Agents borrowing sessions or holding broad credentials escalate beyond their mandate.

owasp.name: Agentic Supply Chain Vulnerabilities
owasp.summary: Agents install or fetch dependencies and packages that were planted or typosquatted.

owasp.name: Unexpected Code Execution
owasp.summary: Code-execution surfaces (interpreters, shells) are turned into arbitrary command execution.

owasp.name: Memory & Context Poisoning
owasp.summary: Attacker plants instructions in files, pages or memory the agent later trusts.

owasp.name: Insecure Inter-Agent Communication
owasp.summary: Unvalidated agent-to-agent messages and handoffs carry attacker-controlled tasks.

owasp.name: Cascading Failures
owasp.summary: Small errors (a hallucinated vendor, a wrong amount) propagate into real-world actions.

owasp.name: Human-Agent Trust Exploitation
owasp.summary: Fake authority ('the CEO approved this over WhatsApp') drives unauthorized actions.

owasp.name: Rogue Agents
owasp.summary: Compromised or misaligned agents cover their tracks: erasing logs, disabling audit.
